claims.text: Pod cart-74587775fc-4rdzm (namespace astronomy-shop) is Running but not ready and crash-looping: container cart restart count went 1 -> 3 -> 4 and its last termination reason is Error with exit code 139.

The cart container's own log shows 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' raised in cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected (ValkeyCartStore.cs:line 101) via Initialize() and Program.<Main>$, at 02:20:00 and again at 02:20:06.

Kubelet recorded 'Back-off restarting failed container cart in pod cart-74587775fc-4rdzm_astronomy-shop' at 02:20:06, and cart Deployments show no OOMKilled or Evicted mark (last termination reason is Error/139).

The Endpoints object for Service cart (ClusterIP 10.96.193.201, port 8080) contains only a notReadyAddresses entry for pod cart-74587775fc-4rdzm (IP 10.244.234.157, node sregym-worker), so the Service has no ready backend.

The synthetic load generator observed the user-visible failure: its log at 02:19:58 reports HTTP 500 Server Error on POST /api/cart (3 occurrences) and POST /api/checkout (1) with fail_ratio 0.1739.

Dependency valkey-cart is Running and Ready with 0 restarts, started 02:19:10, logged 'Ready to accept connections tcp' on port 6379, and its Service valkey-cart has a ready endpoint address 10.244.7.213:6379 on node sregym-worker2.

The preceding cart pod cart-74587775fc-r84cf (same ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc, node sregym-worker3) logged 'Successfully connected to Redis' at 02:19:17.325 and handled GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync/EmptyCartAsync until 02:19:52; it then logged 'Application is shutting down...' and the kubelet event 'Stopping container cart' at 02:19:53, after which ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc created cart-74587775fc-4rdzm, scheduled on sregym-worker.

The failing pod's own init container established a TCP connection to the valkey Service: its log line 'valkey-cart (10.96.223.106:6379) open' is timestamped 02:19:54.300, about six seconds before the cart container's first 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' failure at 02:20:00.

cart and valkey-cart Deployments were created by the helm manager at 02:19:07 with metadata.generation 1 and no later spec write (only status updates by kube-controller-manager), and the cart Deployment's template sets VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-cart, and init container wait-for-valkey-cart.

Resource usage stayed under limits: the cart container's peak memory was 101,560,320 bytes against a 167,772,160-byte (160Mi) limit, valkey-cart's peak was 5,386,240 bytes against a 67,108,864-byte (64Mi) limit, and max_over_time(container_oom_events_total) over 2h was 0 for every container in the namespace.

No NetworkPolicies existed in the cluster at query time (the kind returned zero objects), and the cart Service selector opentelemetry.io/name=cart and valkey-cart selector opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart both resolve to the expected pods via their Endpoints.

The flagd fault-injection configuration in ConfigMap flagd-config has every flag at defaultVariant 'off', including cartFailure, failedReadinessProbe, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, adFailure, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure.
valkey-cart shows no failure signal of its own: 0 restarts, Ready, listener log, ready endpoint, 5.4 MB used and no OOM events - so a valkey crash or OOM is not what the evidence shows.

A cluster-wide Valkey or cart-manifest problem is counter-indicated: the previous cart pod from the same ReplicaSet connected to Redis successfully at 02:19:17 and served traffic until 02:19:52, and both cart and valkey-cart Deployments are at generation 1 with no spec change after the 02:19:07 helm apply.

A plain TCP blackhole from the failing cart pod to the valkey Service is contradicted by that pod's own init container reporting the connection to 10.96.223.106:6379 as open at 02:19:54, six seconds before the first failure.

OOM as the crash mechanism is rejected: the container's last termination reason is Error (exit 139), not OOMKilled, peak memory was 101.5 MB under the 160Mi limit, and container_oom_events_total stayed 0 for every container in astronomy-shop.
A flagd-injected cart failure is rejected: all flags in flagd-config, including cartFailure and failedReadinessProbe, have defaultVariant off.

A valkey-cart crash/restart is rejected as the cause of cart's Redis failure: valkey-cart-859985f49d-shtsv has 0 restarts, started 02:19:10, logged 'Ready to accept connections tcp', and its endpoint address is ready.

Candidate 1 (unresolved): valkey-cart may accept TCP but not complete the Redis handshake (for example a wedged/blocked server process), so StackExchange.Redis' ConnectionMultiplexer.Connect times out and the app throws 'Wasn't able to connect to redis'. This would explain the init container's successful TCP connect and valkey's unchanged restart count, but it is unverified: the Redis integration rejected the configured credentials (REDIS_AUTH_FAILED) for both redis_info and redis_config_get, and no pod exec or post-02:20:14 valkey log is available.

Candidate 2 (unresolved): something specific to the replacement pod's runtime path (for example name resolution, or CNI/kube-proxy state on node sregym-worker at the moment the pod started) keeps the .NET client from completing the Redis connection, even though the busybox init container of the same pod completed a TCP connect moments earlier. Partially contradicted by that init container result and by the fact that other workloads on sregym-worker (for example locust-fetcher) used ClusterIP services in the same window.

Candidate 3 (unresolved): the termination of cart-74587775fc-r84cf at 02:19:53 by an actor outside the ReplicaSet (no SuccessfulDelete, no eviction or OOM mark, only kubelet 'Stopping container cart') removed the only working cart replica and exposed that newly started cart pods cannot establish the Redis connection. The deletion is a mechanism that started the outage, not the reason the replacement cannot start.

Verify the Valkey side directly before changing anything: read valkey-cart's logs after 02:20:14, confirm requirepass/protected-mode/maxmemory and answer a PING/INFO from the cart pod's network namespace, and check that the Redis credentials configured for the observability integration belong to valkey-cart (the integration currently fails with REDIS_AUTH_FAILED).

Inspect node sregym-worker's CNI/kube-proxy state for the cart pod's veth and re-test cart-to-valkey connectivity from inside the cart container, since the init container's TCP check and the app's Redis connect disagree.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
